gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: He drives ___ old van that is always breaking down.
gaps.explanation: 'An old van' — 'old' begins with a vowel sound. The second gap is 'the axle'.
Plural general nouns and flu (illness name) take no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
gaps.explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: I downloaded ___ MP3 file from the band's website.
gaps.explanation: 'MP3' is pronounced /em/, a vowel sound, so 'an'.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: She was wearing ___ old denim jacket that I loved at first sight.
gaps.explanation: 'An old…' — 'old' starts with a vowel sound.
